   364	\subsection{Expanding the Hilbert space and defining commuting observables}
   365	\label{sec:expanding}
   366	
   367	\paragraph{Expanded state.} We introduce registers $\alice', \alice'', \bob', \bob''$ that are each isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$. Define the state \begin{equation}\label{eq:def-psihat}
   368		\ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''} = (\ket{\psi})_{\alice \bob} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice' \alice''} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\bob' \bob''}\;,
   369	\end{equation}
   370	where we have added maximally entangled states in registers
   371	$\alice' \alice''$ and $\bob' \bob''$; recall also that the state $\ket{\psi}$ is already implicitly  appended with sufficiently many ancilla qubits initialized in the $\ket{0}$ state. 
   372	For the remainder of the Appendix all approximations will be evaluated with respect to this state.
   373	
   374	\paragraph{Expanded observables.} For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, $r \in \F_q$, and $u \in \F_q^m$ define the following observable $\hat{W}^r(u)$: \begin{equation}\label{eq:lc-23}
   375		\hat{W}^r(u) = W^r(u) \otimes \tau^W(r \cdot \ind_m(u))\;,
   376	\end{equation}
   377	where $W^r(u)$ is the observable defined in \Cref{eq:qld-strat-obs} and $\tau^W(r \cdot \ind_m(u))$ is the generalized Pauli observable (see \Cref{sec:generalized-pauli}) acting on $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$. 
   378	
   379	For $a\in \F_q$ define corresponding projections
   380	\[
   381		\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a = \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \hat{W}^r(u)\;.
   382	\]
   383	Note that $\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a$ can be equivalently
   384	written as a sum of projectors by applying Fourier
   385	identities. Specifically, for $W \in \{X, Z\}$, $u \in \F_q^{m}$, and
   386	$a \in \F_q$, define the projector
   387	\begin{equation} \tau^{W, u}_{a} =
   388	  \tau^{W}_{[ g_{\cdot}(u) = a]} = \sum_{h \in \F_q^{\nqubits}: h
   389	    \cdot \ind_m(u) = a} \tau^{W}_{h}\;. \label{eq:qld-point-obs-def} \end{equation}
   390	Then we can write $\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_a$ as follows:
   391	\begin{align*}
   392	  \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a
   393	  &= \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \,
   394	    W^r(u) \otimes \tau^W(r
   395	    \cdot \ind_m(u)) \\
   396	    &= \E_{r \in \F_q}
   397	    (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \Big(\sum_{a' \in \F_q}(-1)^{\tr (a' r)} M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}
   398	    \Big) \otimes \Big(
   399	    \sum_{h \in \F_q^n}
   400	    (-1)^{\tr( r( h \cdot \ind_m(u)))} \tau^{W}_{h} \Big) \\
   401	  &= \E_{r \in \F_q}
   402	    (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \Big(\sum_{a' \in \F_q}(-1)^{\tr (a' r)} M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}
   403	    \Big) \otimes \Big(
   404	    \sum_{a'' \in \F_q}
   405	    (-1)^{\tr(a'' r)} \tau^{W,u}_{a''} \Big) \\
   406	  &=	\sum_{a',a'' \in \F_q} \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr((a + a' + a'')r)} \, M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}  \otimes \tau^{W,u}_{a''} \\
   407	  &= \sum_{\substack{a',a'' \in \F_q \\ a' + a'' = a}}  \, M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'}  \otimes \tau^{W,u}_{a''}\;,
   408	\end{align*}
   409	where in the second line we have used \Cref{eq:qld-strat-obs} on the
   410	first tensor factor and \Cref{eq:pauli-obs-proj} on the second, and in the third line we
   411	have used \Cref{eq:qld-point-obs-def}.
   412	For a fixed $u\in\F_q^m$, $r \in \F_q$ and $b \in \F_2$, define a projection
   413	\begin{equation}
   414		\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u,r}_b = \sum_{a \in \F_q : \tr(ar) = b}
   415	        \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a\;, \label{eq:qld-def-mptur}
   416	\end{equation}
   417	which can be equivalently written as
   418	\begin{equation}\label{eq:lc-22}
   419	\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u,r}_b = \frac{1}{2} \Big ( \Id + (-1)^b \hat{W}^r(u) \Big)\;.
   420	\end{equation}
   421	
   422	The registers that the operators $\hat{W}^r(u)$,
   423	$\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a$, and $\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u,r}_b$ act on
   424	depend on context. For example if $W^r(u)$ is viewed as an operator
   425	acting on register $\alice$, then we will view $\hat{W}^r(u)$ as
   426	acting on registers $\alice \alice'$ (with the $\tau^W$ observable
   427	acting on register $\alice'$). We generally indicate via subscripts
   428	which registers the operators act on (for example we will write
   429	$(\hat{W}^r(u))_{\alice \alice'}$ or $(\hat{W}^r(u))_{\bob
   430	  \alice''}$).
   431	
   432	
   433	
   434	\paragraph{Partitioning the registers, and symmetries}
   435	In the remainder of this section as well as \Cref{sec:combining,sec:apply-ldt}, we will partition the six registers
   436	$\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''$ into
   437	two ``parties'' in two different ways. The first is to consider
   438	$\alice \alice'$ together to form  a single party, and $\bob \alice''$
   439	to form the second party. The second is to consider $\bob \bob'$ to
   440	form the first party, and $\alice \bob''$ to form the second
   441	party. Thanks to the symmetry of the Pauli basis test under exchanging the
   442	two players, as well as the symmetry of the ancilla states in
   443	registers $\alice' \alice''$ and $\bob' \bob''$, every ``bipartite'' consistency relation we derive between two
   444	operators $M, N$ will hold for both of the two bipartitioning schemes,
   445	and with the first and second party interchanged. That is, whenever we
   446	derive a bipartite relation of the form
   447	\[ M_{\alice \alice'} \approx_\delta N_{\bob \alice''}, \]
   448	the same steps, with the registers appropriately changed, will also
   449	yield
   450	\begin{align*}
   451	  N_{\alice \alice'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\bob \alice''}, \\
   452	  M_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} N_{\alice \bob''}, \\
   453	  N_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\alice \bob''}.
   454	\end{align*}
   455	
   456	Similarly, whenever we derive a single-party relation of the form
   457	$M_{\alice \alice'} \approx N_{\alice \alice'}$, the same steps with
   458	the registers appropriately changed will also yield the same relation
   459	on $\bob\alice''$, $\bob \bob'$ and $\alice \bob''$. We refer to these
   460	relations as \emph{symmetric equivalents}.
   461	
   462	\begin{lemma}
   463	\label{lem:qld-comm-cons}
   464		There exists a function $\delta_{\acom}(\eps) = \poly(\eps)$ such that the following holds. 
   465	
   466	
   467	\begin{enumerate}
   468		\item (\textbf{Self-consistency}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on average over $r \in \F_q$ and $u\in \F_q^m$, we have 
   469		\[
   470			(\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a)_{\alice \alice'} \approx_\eps (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a)_{\bob \alice''}\,.
   471			\]
   472		\item (\textbf{Approximate commutation}) On average over
   473	          uniformly random $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$,
   474	          we have 
   475		\[
   476			(\hat{M}^{(\Point,\xpt),u_\xpt,r_\xpt}_{b}
   477	                \hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),u_\zpt,r_\zpt}_{b'})_{\alice
   478	                  \alice'} \approx_{\delta_{\acom}}
   479	                (\hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),u_\zpt,r_\zpt}_{b'}
   480	                \hat{M}^{(\Point,\xpt),u_\xpt,r_\xpt}_{b})_{\alice
   481	                  \alice'} \;.
   482		\]
   483	      \end{enumerate}
   484	      Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations
   485	      also hold.
   486	\end{lemma}
   487	
   488	\begin{proof}
   489	Item 1, the self-consistency of $\{\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a \}$, follows from the fact that the original points measurements $\{ M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \}$ are approximately self-consistent between registers $\alice$ and $\bob$ in $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$ (item~\ref{enu:qld-cons} in Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}), the Pauli projections $\{\tau^W_a(\ind_m(u))\}$ are perfectly self-consistent between registers $\alice'$ and $\alice''$, and~\Cref{fact:data-processing}. 
   490		
   491		We now establish the approximate commutation relations. On average over uniformly random $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, we have
   492		\begin{align*}
   493		&\hat{M}^{(\Point,\xpt),u_\xpt,r_\xpt}_{b} \hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),u_\zpt,r_\zpt}_{b'}  \label{eq:qld-m-x-m-z} \\
   494		&= \frac{1}{4} \Big ( \Id + (-1)^b \hat{X}^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt) \Big ) \Big ( \Id + (-1)^{b'} \hat{Z}^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \Big ) \\
   495		&= \frac{1}{4} \Big ( \Id + (-1)^b \hat{X}^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt) + (-1)^{b'} \hat{Z}^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) + (-1)^{b + b'} \hat{X}^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt) \hat{Z}^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \Big)\;,
   496		\end{align*}
   497		where the first equality follows from~\eqref{eq:lc-22}.	
   498		Note that
   499		\begin{align*}
   500		\hat{X}^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt)
   501	         & \hat{Z}^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \\
   502					&=
   503	                                             X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt)
   504	                                             Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt)
   505	                                             \otimes \tau^X(r_\xpt
   506	                                             \cdot \ind_m(u_\xpt))
   507	                                             \tau^Z(r_\zpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt)) \\
   508		&\approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt)
   509	   X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt)  \otimes \tau^Z(r_\zpt\cdot \ind_m( u_\zpt))
   510	   \tau^X(r_\xpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\xpt)) \\
   511		&= \hat{Z}^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \hat{X}^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt)\;, 
   512		\end{align*}
   513		where the first equality follows from~\eqref{eq:lc-23} and for the second line we used the approximate (anti-)commutation
   514	        relation~\eqref{eq:pts-obs-commutation} for the
   515	        $X^{r_\xpt}(u_\xpt)$ and  $Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt)$
   516	        observables, as well as the exact (anti-)commutation relations
   517	        for the $\tau^Z(r_\zpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt))$ and
   518	        $\tau^X(r_\xpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\xpt))$ observables. This shows
   519	        the desired approximate commutation relation, with
   520	        $\delta_{\acom} = \sqrt{\eps}$.
   521	\end{proof}
   522	
   523	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:qld-comm-line-cons}
   524	There exists a function $\delta_{\Line}(\eps) = \poly(\eps)$ such that the following holds. 
   525		For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and lines $\line$ there exists a projective measurement $\{ \hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f \}_{f \in \deg_{md}(\line)}$, acting on registers $\alice\alice'$ or $\bob\alice''$, such that:
   526		\begin{enumerate}
   527			\item  (\textbf{Self-consistency})\label{enu:qld-comm-line-self-cons}  For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and $r \in \F_q$, on average over a uniformly random  pair $(\line, u)$
   528	                drawn from the line-point distribution
   529	                (\Cref{def:line-point-dist}),
   530			\[
   531				(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_\Line} (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\bob \alice''}\;.
   532			\]
   533			
   534			\item (\textbf{Consistency with points measurements I}) \label{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons}
   535			On average over a uniformly random pair $(\line, u)$
   536	                drawn from the line-point distribution, 
   537			\[
   538				(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_\Line} (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{f(u)})_{\bob \alice''}\;.
   539			\]		
   540			\item (\textbf{Consistency with points measurements II}) \label{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2}
   541			On average over a uniformly random pair $(\line, u)$
   542	                drawn from the line-point distribution,
   543			\[
   544				(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_\Line}  (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\;.
   545			\]
   546	              \end{enumerate}
   547	                    Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations
   548	      also hold.
   549	\end{lemma}
   550	
   551	\begin{proof}
   552		Define the operator
   553		\[
   554			\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f = \sum_{\substack{f',f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line) : \\ f' + f'' = f}} M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{f'} \otimes \tau^{W,\line}_{f''}\;,
   555		\]
   556		where the Pauli operator $\tau^{W,\line}_{f''}$ acting on register $\alice'$ is obtained by measuring all $\nqubits$ qudits in the basis $W$ to obtain an outcome $h \in \F_q^\nqubits$ and then returning the restriction $f''$ of $g_h: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ to the line $\line$. Here, $g_h$ is the degree-$d$ low-degree extension of $h$ defined in~\eqref{eq:ld-encoding}. 
   557		
   558		\Cref{enu:qld-comm-line-self-cons},	the self-consistency of $\{\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f \}$, follows from the fact that the original lines measurement $\{ M^{(\Line,W),\line}_f \}$ is self-consistent between registers $\alice$ and $\bob$ in $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$ (\Cref{enu:qld-cons} in Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}), the Pauli projections $\{\tau^{W,\line}_{f''}\}$ are perfectly self-consistent on between registers $\alice'$ and $\alice''$, and~\Cref{fact:data-processing}. 
   559	
   560	\Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons}, the consistency with the points measurements, follows because on average over $(\line,u)$ drawn from the line-point distribution we have
   561	\begin{align}
   562		&(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \\
   563		&= \sum_{\substack{f',f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line) : \\ f' + f'' =
   564	  f}} (M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{f'} \otimes \tau^{W,\line}_{f''})_{\alice
   565	  \alice'} \\
   566	        &= \sum_{\substack{f', f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line): \\ f' + f'' =
   567	  f}} ((M^{(\Line, W), \line}_{f'} \otimes \tau^{W, \line}_{f''})
   568	  \cdot (M^{(\Line, W), \line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = f'(u)]} )_{\alice
   569	  \alice'} \label{eq:qld-mhat-line-1} \\
   570		&\approx_\eps \sum_{\substack{f',f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line) : \\
   571	  f' + f'' = f}} (M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{f'} \otimes
   572	  \tau^{W,\line}_{f''})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes
   573	  (M^{(\Point,W),u}_{f'(u)})_{\bob
   574	  \alice''} \label{eq:qld-mhat-line-2} \\
   575	  	&= \sum_{\substack{f',f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line) : \\ f' + f'' =
   576	  f}} (M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{f'} \otimes \tau^{W,\line}_{f''})_{\alice
   577	  \alice'} \otimes (M^{(\Point,W),u}_{f'(u)} \otimes
   578	  \tau^{W,u}_{f''(u)})_{\bob \alice''} \label{eq:qld-mhat-line-3} \\
   579		&= \sum_{\substack{f',f'' \in \deg_{md}(\line) : \\ f' + f'' =
   580	  f}} (M^{(\Line,W),\line}_{f'} \otimes \tau^{W,\line}_{f''})_{\alice
   581	  \alice'} \otimes \Big (\sum_{\substack{a', a'' : \\ a' + a'' = f'(u)
   582	  + f''(u)}}  M^{(\Point,W),u}_{a'} \otimes \tau^{W,u}_{a''} \Big
   583	  )_{\bob \alice''} \label{eq:qld-mhat-line-4} \\
   584		&= (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes
   585	   (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{f(u)})_{\bob \alice''}\;. \label{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons-eps}
   586	\end{align}
   587	\Cref{eq:qld-mhat-line-1} follows from the projectivity of
   588	$\{\hat{M}^{(\Line, W), \line}_{f}\}$. \Cref{eq:qld-mhat-line-2} follows from the consistency between the line
   589	and point measurements (\Cref{enu:qld-ld} in
   590	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}) together with
   591	\Cref{fact:add-a-proj2}. \Cref{eq:qld-mhat-line-3}
   592	follows from the exact consistency between the $\{ \tau^{W,\line}_{f''} \}$ and $\{
   593	\tau^{W,u}_{f''(u)} \}$ measurements on the $\alice'$ and $\alice''$ registers. \Cref{eq:qld-mhat-line-4} follows because
   594	the consistency of the $\tau$ measurements force $a' = f'(u)$ and $a''
   595	= f''(u)$ . This establishes \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons}, with
   596	approximation error $\eps$.
   597	
   598	To show \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2} we would like to first
   599	apply~\Cref{fact:data-processing} to \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons-eps},
   600	to sum over all functions $f$ that evaluate to the same value at a given
   601	point $u$. Unfortunately, we cannot use the Fact as written, since the
   602	bound in \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons} is in terms of $\approx$, not
   603	$\simeq$, and moreover the right-hand side does not have the form $I
   604	\ot B$. Instead, we show the desired bound by direct calculation from \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons-eps}
   605	\begin{align}
   606	  \eps &\geq \E_{\omega} \sum_{f} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Line, W),
   607	  \line}_f )^2 \ot (I - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{f(u)})^2 \ket{\hat{\psi}}
   608	  \\
   609	                 &= \E_{\omega} \sum_{f} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \hat{M}^{(\Line, W),
   610	                   \line}_f  \ot (I - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{f(u)})
   611	                   \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
   612	                 &= \E_{\omega} \sum_{a} \sum_{f: f(u) = a} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \hat{M}^{(\Line, W),
   613	                   \line}_f  \ot (I - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})
   614	                   \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
   615	                 &=\E_{\omega} \sum_{a}  \bra{\hat{\psi}} \hat{M}^{(\Line, W),
   616	                   \line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]}  \ot (I - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})
   617	                   \ket{\hat{\psi}},
   618	\end{align}
   619	where in going to the second line we have used the projectivity of the
   620	measurements $\{\hat{M}^{(\Line, W), \line}_f\}$ and
   621	$\{\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a}\}$.
   622	Thus, we have deduced that
   623	\begin{equation}
   624	\label{eq:qld-comm-line-1}
   625	(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \approx_\eps (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\;.
   626	\end{equation}
   627	Since both the $\{ \hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_f\}$ and $\{ \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a \}$ measurements are projective, we also get 
   628	\begin{align}
   629	\Id &= \sum_a (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) =
   630	      a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes I_{\bob \alice''}\notag\\
   631	&= \sum_a \Big((\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) =
   632	                                                               a]})_{\alice
   633	                                                               \alice'}
   634	                                                               \ot
   635	                                                               I_{\bob
   636	                                                               \alice''}-(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\Big) \notag\\
   637	&\qquad\qquad + \sum_a (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\;.\label{eq:com-1a}
   638	\end{align}
   639	For projective sub-measurements $\{A_i\}$ and $\{B_i\}$ and a state $\ket{\varphi}$,
   640	\begin{align*}
   641	\sum_i \bra{\varphi}\big(A_i-B_i\big)\ket{\varphi} &= \sum_i \bra{\varphi}A_i(A_i-B_i)\ket{\varphi} + \sum_i \bra{\varphi}(A_i-B_i)B_i\ket{\varphi}\\
   642	&\leq \Big(\sum_i \bra{\varphi}A_i^2\ket{\varphi} \Big)^{1/2}\Big(\sum_i \bra{\varphi}(A_i-B_i)^2\ket{\varphi}\Big)^{1/2} \\
   643	&\qquad\qquad+ \Big(\sum_i \bra{\varphi}(A_i-B_i)^2 \ket{\varphi}\Big)^{1/2}\Big(\sum_i \bra{\varphi}B_i^2\ket{\varphi}\Big)^{1/2}\\
   644	&\leq 2\Big(\sum_i \bra{\varphi}(A_i-B_i)^2 \ket{\varphi}\Big)^{1/2}\;.

   646	Applying this fact to the projective sub-measurements $\{(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'}\}_a$ and $\{(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\}$ in~\eqref{eq:com-1a} and using~\eqref{eq:qld-comm-line-1} gives
   647	\begin{equation}
   648	\label{eq:qld-comm-line-2}
   649		\Id \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} \sum_a (\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\;.
   650	      \end{equation}
   651	      To go from~\eqref{eq:qld-comm-line-2} to \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2} of the lemma we use another fact about
   652	      projective measurements. For families of projective measurements $\{A^x_i\}$
   653	      and $\{B^x_i\}$ acting on separate registers of a bipartite state
   654	      $\ket{\phi}$, suppose $I \approx_{\delta} \sum_i A^x_i \ot B^x_i$. Then
   655	      \begin{align*}
   656	        \delta &\geq \E_{x} \Big\| \Big(\Id - \sum_i A^x_i \ot B^x_i\Big) \ket{\phi}\Big\|^2  \\
   657	               &= \E_{x} \Big(1 + \bra{\phi} \Big(\sum_i A^x_i \ot
   658	                 B^x_i\Big)^2 \ket{\phi} - 2 \sum_i \bra{\phi} A^x_i \ot B^x_i
   659	                 \ket{\phi} \Big) \\
   660	               &= 1 - \E_{x} \sum_i \bra{\phi} A^x_i \ot B^x_i \ket{\phi}\;,
   661	\end{align*}
   662	      where we used the projectivity in going from the second to
   663	      the third line, to remove the square. Thus
   664	      \[ \E_{x} \sum_{i \neq j} \bra{\phi} A^x_i \ot B^x_j \ket{\phi} \leq
   665	        \delta\;, \]
   666	      and $A^x_i \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot B^x_i$. By
   667	      Item~1 of \Cref{fact:agreement}, this in turn implies that $A^x_i \ot I
   668	      \approx_\delta I \ot B^x_i$. Applying this fact to the projective
   669	      measurements $\{ (\hat{M}^{(\Line, W), \line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) =
   670	        a]})_{\alice \alice'} \}_a$ and $\{(\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),
   671	        u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\}$ in~\eqref{eq:qld-comm-line-2} gives
   672	      \[
   673		(\hat{M}^{(\Line,W),\line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]})_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}.
   674	      \]
   675	      Taking the function $\delta_{\Line}$ in the lemma to be $\sqrt{\eps}$,
   676	      this yields the conclusion of \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2}
   677	      of the lemma.
   678	\end{proof}

    51	\begin{definition}
    52	Given integer $d,m$ and a prime power $q$ we denote by $\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ the set of polynomials in $m$ variables
    53	  with \emph{individual} degree at most $d$ in each variable. When the field is clear from context we write $\ideg_{d,m}$. 	
    54		When
    55	  the number of variables is clear from context we
    56	  write $\ideg_d$. We denote by $\deg_{d}$ the set of polynomials with
    57	  \emph{total} degree at most $d$.
    58	\end{definition}
    59	
    60	Recall the low-degree code defined in \Cref{sec:ld-encoding}, in which vectors $h \in \F_q^\nqubits$ get mapped to polynomials $g_h \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ such that for every $u \in \{0,1\}^m$, $g_h(u) = h_u$ where the coordinates of $h$ are indexed by binary strings of length $m$. For $x\in \F_q^m$, recall the definition of the vector $\ind_m(x) \in \F_q^\nqubits$ from Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}. Recall also the finite field trace $\tr(\cdot)=\tr_{q\to 2}(\cdot):\F_q\to\F_2$, where $q=2^k$ for odd $k$, defined in Section~\ref{sec:subfields}. 
    61	
    62	
    63	
    64	Call a tuple $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) \in (\F_q^m)^2
    65	\times (\F_q)^2$ \emph{anticommuting} if the quantity 
    66	 \[\gamma\,=\,\tr ((r_\xpt \cdot
    67	\ind_m(u_\xpt)) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt)))\]
    68	introduced in~\Cref{eq:gamma-value} is not $0$, and \emph{commuting} if $\gamma=0$.
    69	
    70	\begin{fact}
    71	\label{fact:omega-anticomm-prob}
    72		The probability that a tuple $\omega= (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$ sampled uniformly at random from $(\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$
    73		is anti-commuting is at least 
    74		\[
    75			(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot \Big (1 - \frac{md}{q} \Big )  \cdot \frac{1}{2} \geq \Big (1 - \frac{3md}{q} \Big ) \cdot \frac{1}{2}.
    76		\]
    77		The probability that $\omega$ is commuting is also at least $\Big(1 - \frac{3md}{q} \Big ) \cdot \frac{1}{2}$.
    78	\end{fact}
    79	\begin{proof}
    80		First, note that $\ind_m(u_\xpt) = 0$ if and only if $u_\xpt = 0$. If $u_\xpt=0$ then $\omega$ is commuting. Otherwise, if $u_\xpt \neq 0$, then observe that for all $r_\xpt, r_\zpt, u_\zpt$,
    81		\begin{align*}
    82			\tr( (r_\xpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\xpt)) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot
    83	                \ind_m(u_\zpt))) &= \tr( r_\xpt r_\zpt (\ind_m(u_\xpt) \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt))) \\
    84									&= \tr( (r_\xpt r_\zpt) \cdot g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt))\;,
    85		\end{align*}
    86		where $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}$ is a nonzero polynomial in $\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$.
    87		
    88		If $r_\xpt = 0$, then $\omega$ is commuting. Condition on $r_\xpt \neq 0$.  Since $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}\neq 0$ has total degree at most $md$, by the Schwartz-Zippel lemma the probability that $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt)$ is zero over a uniformly random choice of $u_\zpt$ is at most $md/q$. Conditioned on $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt) \neq 0$, the product $(r_\xpt r_\zpt) \cdot g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt)$ is a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ when $r_\zpt$ is chosen uniformly at random. 
    89		
    90		The probability that $u_\xpt \neq 0, r_\xpt \neq 0, g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt) \neq 0$ is at least $(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot (1 - md/q)$ since $u_\xpt, r_\xpt, u_\zpt$ are chosen independently.
    91		
    92		Since $q = 2^t$ is an admissible field size, we have that for all $a \in \F_q$, the trace of $a$ is equal to $\sum_i a_i$ where $(a_1,\ldots,a_t)=\kappa(a) \in \F_2^t$ are defined in Section~\ref{sec:subfields}. Thus the probability that a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ has trace $0$ is exactly $1/2$. 
    93	\end{proof}

    95	In this appendix we often use the ``$\approx_\delta$'' notation to specify closeness of general operators (not necessarily POVMs) that are indexed by questions but not answers: given sets of operators $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ indexed by questions $x \in \cal{X}$, we write $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ to denote \[
    96		\E_{x \sim \mu} \bra{\psi} (A^x - B^x)^\dagger (A^x - B^x)
    97	        \ket{\psi}\,\leq\, O(\delta)
    98	      \]
    99	where $\mu$ is a question distribution and $\ket{\psi}$ is a state that has been fixed by context. This will be useful for expressing closeness of observables, for example. The following two lemmas relate the closeness between sets of operators and weighted sums of those operators. 
   100	\begin{lemma}
   101	\label{lem:avg-closeness}
   102	Let $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ be operators indexed by some finite set $\mathcal{X}$, and let $\mu$ be a probability distribution over $\mathcal{X}$. Let $\{\alpha_x \}$ be a set of complex numbers such that $|\alpha_x| \leq 1$. Then if $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ on average over $x$ drawn from $\mu$, then $A \approx_\delta B$, where $A = \E_x \alpha_x A^x$ and $B= \E_x \alpha_x B^x$.
   103	\end{lemma}
   104	\begin{proof}
   105	Expand
   106	\begin{align*}
   107		\Big\| \E_x \alpha_x \big ( A^x - B^x \big) \ket{\psi} \Big\|^2 &\leq \Big( \E_x \norm{ (A^x -B^x) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   108		&\leq \E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   109		&\leq \delta\;.
   110	\end{align*}
   111	The first inequality is the triangle inequality and the second inequality is Jensen's inequality. 
   112	\end{proof}
   113	
   114	\begin{lemma}
   115	\label{lem:povm-to-obs}
   116	Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set. Let $\{A^x_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ and $\{B^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be POVMs and let $\{ \alpha_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a collection of complex numbers on the unit circle. Let $A^x = \sum_a \alpha_a A^x_a$ and $B^x = \sum_a  \alpha_a B^x_a$. Then 
   117	\[
   118		A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a \quad \text{implies} \quad A^x \approx_{\delta'} B^x
   119	\]
   120	for $\delta' = |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta$.
   121	\end{lemma}
   122	\begin{proof}
   123	Expand
   124		\begin{align*}
   125			\E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 &= \E_x \Big\|\sum_a \alpha_a (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}\Big\|^2 \\
   126			&\leq \E_x \Big( \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   127			&\leq \E_x |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   128			&\leq |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta\;.
   129		\end{align*}
   130	The first inequality follows from the triangle inequality, the second inequality follows from Cauchy-Schwarz, and the last inequality follows from the assumption that $A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a$. 
   131	\end{proof}

   278	                        Z^{r_\zpt}(u_\zpt) \otimes \Id_\bob\notag\\

/-!
# Lines, bounded line polynomials, and line-point distributions

This file provides the seed-bearing line descriptions and coefficient-list
polynomials shared by the observable and combining chapters.  It also realizes
the line-point distribution directly from the conditionally linear sampler.

The bounded multivariate polynomial index remains the actual Mathlib
`polyFunc` subtype.  Its finite instance is derived by injecting it into the
finite table of coefficients with coordinatewise-bounded exponents.

## References

The line and bounded-polynomial interface is `def:ideg-deg-polynomials` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:51-62`.  The line-point sampler
is `def:line-point-dist` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, used in
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:882-1019`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT
open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

noncomputable section

/-- The two presentations of lines used by the low-degree question sampler. -/
inductive LineKind where
  | axis
  | diagonal
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- A line description retains the source seed as well as the canonical base
point and raw direction data.  Retaining `seed` is essential for the restricted
line distributions in the combining argument. -/
structure LineDesc (L : LdParams) where
  kind : LineKind
  base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L
  seed : ScalarQ L
  rawDirection : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The geometric direction represented by a seed-bearing line description. -/
def LineDesc.direction {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    Fin L.m → ScalarQ L :=
  match line.kind with
  | .axis => coordinateDirection (chiIndex L line.seed)
  | .diagonal => prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.rawDirection

/-- The point set represented by a seed-bearing line description. -/
def LineDesc.pointSet {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    Set (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :=
  linePoints line.base line.direction

/-- Coefficient-list representation of a univariate polynomial of degree at
most `c` over the scalar field of `L`. -/
abbrev DegPoly (L : LdParams) (c : ℕ) := Fin (c + 1) → ScalarQ L

/-- Evaluate a bounded coefficient-list polynomial. -/
def degPolyEval {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ}
    (f : DegPoly L c) (t : ScalarQ L) : ScalarQ L :=
  ∑ i : Fin (c + 1), f i * t ^ i.val

/-- Extend a coefficient list by zero from degree bound `c` to `c'`. -/
def DegPoly.padTo {L : LdParams} {c c' : ℕ} (_h : c ≤ c')
    (f : DegPoly L c) : DegPoly L c' :=
  fun i =>
    if hi : i.val < c + 1 then f ⟨i.val, hi⟩ else 0

/-- A line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` has a line parameter
and every such parameter gives the same value.  The universal clause handles
the zero-direction presentation without choosing a sentinel parameter. -/
def EvaluatesTo {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
    (f : DegPoly L c) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (a : ScalarQ L) : Prop :=
  (∃ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
    ∀ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction → degPolyEval f t = a

/-- Evaluate a line polynomial at a point, returning `none` precisely when the
point does not determine an evaluation.  The `Option` completion is the
paper's bottom outcome for malformed or nonincident answers. -/
noncomputable def evalOpt {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (f : DegPoly L c) : Option (ScalarQ L) := by
  classical
  exact if h : ∃ a : ScalarQ L, EvaluatesTo line f u a then
    some (Classical.choose h)
  else none

/-- Convert an axis-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation. -/
def aLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L where
  kind := .axis
  base := line.point
  seed := line.seed
  rawDirection := 0

/-- Convert a diagonal-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation. -/
def dLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L where
  kind := .diagonal
  base := line.point
  seed := line.seed
  rawDirection := line.direction

/-- The affine-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler. -/
noncomputable def aLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
  (clDistribution (ldALineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
    (aLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)

/-- The diagonal-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler. -/
noncomputable def dLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
  (clDistribution (ldDLineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
    (dLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)

/-- The equal mixture of affine and diagonal line-point samples.  The
parameter record is explicit, so the same definition works at every dimension. -/
noncomputable def linePointDist (L : LdParams) :
    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
  Distribution.mixture (uniformDistribution Bool) fun chooseAxis =>
    if chooseAxis then aLinePointDist L else dLinePointDist L

/-- The affine line-point component has total probability one. -/
theorem aLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
    (aLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
  sorry

/-- The diagonal line-point component has total probability one. -/
theorem dLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
    (dLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
  sorry

/-- The line-point mixture has total probability one. -/
theorem linePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
    (linePointDist L).IsProbability := by
  sorry

/-- Convert a bounded exponent table to the finitely supported exponent vector
used by `MvPolynomial.coeff`. -/
def boundedExponent {m d : ℕ} (e : Fin m → Fin (d + 1)) : Fin m →₀ ℕ :=
  Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun i => (e i).val

/-- The finite coefficient table of a low-individual-degree polynomial. -/
def polyFuncCoeffTable {m d : ℕ} {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
    (p : ↥(polyFunc m K d)) : (Fin m → Fin (d + 1)) → K :=
  fun e => MvPolynomial.coeff (boundedExponent e) p.1

/-- Bounded coefficient tables separate low-individual-degree polynomial
representatives.  This is a formalization-only finiteness lemma. -/
theorem polyFuncCoeffTable_injective {m d : ℕ} {K : Type*}
    [CommSemiring K] : Function.Injective
      (polyFuncCoeffTable : ↥(polyFunc m K d) → (Fin m → Fin (d + 1)) → K) := by
  intro p q hpq
  apply Subtype.ext
  apply MvPolynomial.ext
  intro exponent
  by_cases hbounded : ∀ i : Fin m, exponent i ≤ d
  · let e : Fin m → Fin (d + 1) := fun i => ⟨exponent i, Nat.lt_succ_iff.mpr (hbounded i)⟩
    have hexponent : boundedExponent e = exponent := by
      ext i
      simp [boundedExponent, e]
    have hcoeff := congrFun hpq e
    simpa [polyFuncCoeffTable, hexponent] using hcoeff
  · simp only [not_forall, not_le] at hbounded
    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hbounded
    have hpzero : MvPolynomial.coeff exponent p.1 = 0 := by
      by_contra hpne
      have hmem : exponent ∈ p.1.support := MvPolynomial.mem_support_iff.mpr hpne
      have hle := (MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree
        (σ := Fin m) (R := K) p.1 d).mp p.2 exponent hmem i
      omega
    have hqzero : MvPolynomial.coeff exponent q.1 = 0 := by
      by_contra hqne
      have hmem : exponent ∈ q.1.support := MvPolynomial.mem_support_iff.mpr hqne
      have hle := (MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree
        (σ := Fin m) (R := K) q.1 d).mp q.2 exponent hmem i
      omega
    rw [hpzero, hqzero]

/-- The actual bounded `polyFunc` subtype is finite over a finite coefficient
semiring. -/
noncomputable instance polyFuncFintype (m d : ℕ) (K : Type*)
    [CommSemiring K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] :
    Fintype ↥(polyFunc m K d) :=
  Fintype.ofInjective polyFuncCoeffTable polyFuncCoeffTable_injective

end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

/-!
# State-dependent consistency and operator distance

This file gives the concrete finite-dimensional quantities denoted by
state-dependent consistency and approximate operator equality in the QPBT
analysis.

## References

The consistency functional is `def:consistency` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex`.  The operator
distance is used in
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:680-881`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators ComplexConjugate

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT
open MIPStarRE.Quantum

/-- Average off-diagonal overlap of two outcome-indexed operator families
already placed on a common Hilbert space.  This is `def:consistency`; the
paper's hidden universal constant is carried by the comparison bound, not by
this functional. -/
noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
  avgOver μ fun x =>
    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
      if a = b then 0
      else (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState (A x a * B x b) ψ)).re

/-- The relation denoted `simeq_δ`: the state-dependent consistency defect is
at most `δ`. -/
def IsConsistentWithin {X α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  consistencyDefect μ A B ψ ≤ δ

/-- Average squared state-dependent distance between two single-operator
families.  This is the operator relation used in Chapter 14. -/
noncomputable def opDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → Op ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
  avgOver μ fun x => ‖applyOperatorToState (A x - B x) ψ‖ ^ 2

/-- `opDistSq` is `opFamilyDistSq` for a singleton outcome family.  This is a
formalization-only adapter between the chapter interfaces. -/
theorem opDistSq_eq_opFamilyDistSq_unit {X ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → Op ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    opDistSq μ A B ψ =
      opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => A x) (fun x (_ : Unit) => B x) ψ := by
  simp [opDistSq, opFamilyDistSq]

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT
open MIPStarRE.Quantum

/--
Squared Euclidean distance between pure states.  Blueprint `def:state-distance`
(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-179`), paper origin

    [DecidableEq ι]
    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2

/--
Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,
with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
-/
noncomputable def opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (M x a - N x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   750	\section{Expanding the Hilbert space and defining commuting observables}
   751	\label{sec:expanding}
   752	
   753	The next step of the analysis adjoins ancillary EPR registers to the
   754	players' state and lifts the strategy observables and measurements to the
   755	expanded state. The point of the construction is that the ancilla factor of
   756	each lifted observable carries the \emph{exact} Pauli commutation sign, so
   757	that the signs cancel and the lifted observables approximately commute for
   758	every tuple $\omega$.
   759	
   760	\begin{definition}[Expanded state]
   761		\label{def:expanded-state}
   762		\uses{lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:EPR}
   763		Recall that $M = 2^m$. Introduce registers $\mathsf{A}', \mathsf{A}'',
   764		\mathsf{B}', \mathsf{B}''$, each with Hilbert space isomorphic to
   765		$(\C^q)^{\ot M}$, and define the state
   766		\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-psihat}
   767			\ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''}
   768			\,=\, (\ket{\psi})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}}
   769			\ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''}
   770			\ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''}\,,
   771		\end{equation}
   772		where $\ket{\psi}$ is the extended strategy state of the strategy
   773		under analysis (Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-strategy-setup} and the
   774		convention following it) and
   775		$\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ is the maximally entangled state on
   776		$\C^q \ot \C^q$ (Definition~\ref{def:EPR}). For the remainder of this
   777		chapter, as well as in Chapters~\ref{chap:qpbt-combining}
   778		and~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction}, all approximations $\approx$ and
   779		$\simeq$ are evaluated with respect to the state $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$,
   780		unless stated otherwise.
   781	\end{definition}
   782	
   783	\begin{definition}[Expanded observables]
   784		\label{def:expanded-observables}
   785		\uses{def:strategy-observables, def:expanded-state, lem:twisted-commutation}
   786		For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, $r \in \F_q$, and $u \in \F_q^m$, define the
   787		observable
   788		\begin{equation}\label{eq:lc-23}
   789			\hat{W}^r(u) \,=\, W^r(u) \ot \tau^W(r \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u))\,,
   790		\end{equation}
   791		where $W^r(u)$ is the strategy observable of~\eqref{eq:qld-strat-obs}
   792		and $\tau^W(r \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u))$ is the generalized Pauli
   793		observable acting on $(\C^q)^{\ot M}$, introduced in
   794		Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra}
   795		(see Lemma~\ref{lem:twisted-commutation}). As a product
   796		of two observables with eigenvalues $\pm 1$ acting on disjoint
   797		registers, $\hat{W}^r(u)$ is itself an observable with eigenvalues
   798		$\pm 1$. If $W^r(u)$ is viewed as acting on register $\mathsf{A}$, then
   799		$\hat{W}^r(u)$ is viewed as acting on registers
   800		$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$, with the $\tau^W$ factor acting on
   801		$\mathsf{A}'$. The registers are generally indicated by subscripts, as
   802		in $(\hat{W}^r(u))_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}$ or
   803		$(\hat{W}^r(u))_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$, the latter having the
   804		strategy factor on $\mathsf{B}$ and the Pauli factor on
   805		$\mathsf{A}''$.
   806	\end{definition}
   807	
   808	\begin{definition}[Expanded point measurements]
   809		\label{def:expanded-point-measurement}
   810		\uses{def:expanded-observables, lem:pauli-observable-expansion, def:low-degree-encoding, def:subfield-trace}
   811		For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, $u \in \F_q^m$ and $a \in \F_q$, define
   812		\[
   813			\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \,=\, \E_{r \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(ar)} \, \hat{W}^r(u)\,,
   814		\]
   815		and define the projector
   816		\begin{equation}\label{eq:qld-point-obs-def}
   817			\tau^{W,u}_a \,=\, \tau^W_{[g_\cdot(u) = a]}
   818			\,=\, \sum_{h \in \F_q^{M} \colon h \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = a} \tau^W_h\,,
   819		\end{equation}
   820		where $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^{M}}$ are the joint eigenprojectors of
   821		the generalized Pauli $W$-observables
   822		(see Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-observable-expansion}).
   823		Expanding both tensor factors of $\hat{W}^r(u)$
   824		by~\eqref{eq:qld-strat-obs} and by the Fourier expansion of the
   825		generalized Pauli observables
   826		(see Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-observable-expansion}), and
   827		averaging over $r$, gives the equivalent convolution form
   828		\[
   829			\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a
   830			\,=\, \sum_{\substack{a',a'' \in \F_q \\ a' + a'' = a}}
   831			M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{a'} \ot \tau^{W,u}_{a''}\,.
   832		\]
   833		In particular each $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ is a projection
   834		and $\{\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\}_{a \in \F_q}$ is a projective
   835		measurement.
   836	\end{definition}
   837	
   838	\begin{definition}[Trace-coarse-grained point projections]
   839		\label{def:expanded-point-trace-projection}
   840		\uses{def:expanded-point-measurement, def:expanded-observables, def:subfield-trace}
   841		For fixed $u \in \F_q^m$, $r \in \F_q$ and $b \in \F_2$, define the
   842		projection
   843		\begin{equation}\label{eq:qld-def-mptur}
   844			\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u,r}_b \,=\, \sum_{a \in \F_q \colon \tr(ar) = b} \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\,,
   845		\end{equation}
   846		which can be equivalently written as
   847		\begin{equation}\label{eq:lc-22}
   848			\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u,r}_b \,=\, \frac{1}{2} \Big( \Id + (-1)^b\, \hat{W}^r(u) \Big)\,.
   849		\end{equation}
   850		The register conventions are those of
   851		Definition~\ref{def:expanded-observables}.
   852	\end{definition}

   854	\begin{definition}[Symmetric equivalents]
   855		\label{def:symmetric-equivalents}
   856		\uses{def:expanded-state}
   857		For the remainder of this chapter, as well as in
   858		Chapters~\ref{chap:qpbt-combining} and~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction}, the
   859		six registers
   860		$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''$
   861		are partitioned into two ``parties'' in two different ways. The first
   862		scheme takes $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$ as one party and
   863		$\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''$ as the other; the second scheme takes
   864		$\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'$ as the first party and
   865		$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''$ as the second. The \emph{symmetric
   866		equivalents} of a bipartite relation of the form
   867		$M_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \approx_\delta N_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$
   868		are the three relations
   869		\[
   870			N_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \approx_\delta M_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,,\qquad
   871			M_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'} \approx_\delta N_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''}\,,\qquad
   872			N_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'} \approx_\delta M_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''}\,,
   873		\]
   874		obtained by passing to the second bipartitioning scheme and by
   875		interchanging the first and second party; the symmetric equivalents of
   876		a single-party relation of the form
   877		$M_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \approx N_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}$ are the
   878		same relation on the register pairs $\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''$,
   879		$\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'$ and $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''$.
   880	\end{definition}

   883		\label{lem:symmetric-equivalents-transfer}
   884		\notready
   885		\uses{def:symmetric-equivalents, def:expanded-state, lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:symmetric-game, def:EPR, def:povm-distance}

   887		analysis (Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-strategy-setup} and the convention
   888		following it), assumed symmetric in the sense of
   889		Definition~\ref{def:symmetric-game}: the state $\ket{\psi}$ is
   890		invariant under exchanging registers $\mathsf{A}$ and $\mathsf{B}$, and
   891		both players measure the same operators. Let $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$ be the
   892		expanded state~\eqref{eq:def-psihat}, let

   898			\qquad\qquad

   900			\mathsf{A} \leftrightarrow \mathsf{B},\quad
   901			\mathsf{A}' \leftrightarrow \mathsf{A}''\,,
   902		\]
   903		be the two permutations of the six registers
   904		$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''$
   905		given by these transpositions, and let $U_\sigma$ and $U_\theta$ be the
   906		corresponding permutation unitaries. Write
   907		$\Pi = \{\Id,\, U_\sigma,\, U_\theta,\, U_\sigma U_\theta\}$ and let
   908		\[
   909			\mathcal{R} = \{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}',\; \mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}'',\;
   910			\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}',\; \mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''\}

910			\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}',\; \mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''\}
   911		\]
   912		be the four register placements of
   913		Definition~\ref{def:symmetric-equivalents}. Then:
   914		\begin{enumerate}

   917			\item Let $P$ and $Q$ be operators on
   918			$\hilb \ot (\C^q)^{\ot M}$, where $\hilb$ is the common Hilbert

   920			$\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}', \mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}' \in \mathcal{R}$ and

   925				\bigl\| \bigl( (P)_{U(\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}')} - (Q)_{U(\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}')} \bigr) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \bigr\|\,,

   937		In particular, taking $\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}' = \mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$

   940		$U_\theta$, $U_\sigma$ and $U_\sigma U_\theta$ are exactly the three

   944	\begin{proof}
   945		\uses{def:expanded-state, def:EPR, def:symmetric-game, def:povm-distance}
   946		Each of $\sigma$ and $\theta$ transposes registers carrying isomorphic
   947		Hilbert spaces --- $\mathsf{A}$ and $\mathsf{B}$ both carry $\hilb$,
   948		and the four ancilla registers are all isomorphic to
   949		$(\C^q)^{\ot M}$ (Definition~\ref{def:expanded-state}) --- so the
   950		permutation unitaries $U_\sigma$ and $U_\theta$ are defined and satisfy
   951		$U (P)_{\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}'} U^\dagger = (P)_{U(\mathsf{C})U(\mathsf{C}')}$
   952		for every operator $P$ and every placement.
   953	
   954		For item~1, both generators fix $\ket{\hat{\psi}} = (\ket{\psi})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''}$:
   955		the factor $(\ket{\psi})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}}$ is invariant under
   956		$\mathsf{A} \leftrightarrow \mathsf{B}$ by the symmetry hypothesis;
   957		$\sigma$ exchanges the two ancilla factors, which are identical; and
   958		$\theta$ leaves $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''}$
   959		untouched and exchanges the two halves of each pair in
   960		$\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''}$, under which
   961		$\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ is invariant (Definition~\ref{def:EPR}). The
   962		action on $\mathcal{R}$ sends $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$ to
   963		$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$, $\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'$,
   964		$\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''$ and $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''$ under $\Id$,
   965		$U_\sigma$, $U_\theta$ and $U_\sigma U_\theta$ respectively, so it is
   966		simply transitive on the four placements.
   967	
   968		For item~2, insert $U^\dagger U$ and use $U \ket{\hat{\psi}} = \ket{\hat{\psi}}$
   969		together with unitary invariance of the norm:
   970		\[
   971			\bigl\| \bigl( (P)_{\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}'} - (Q)_{\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}'} \bigr) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \bigr\|
   972			= \bigl\| U \bigl( (P)_{\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}'} - (Q)_{\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}'} \bigr) U^\dagger \, U \ket{\hat{\psi}} \bigr\|
   973			= \bigl\| \bigl( (P)_{U(\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}')} - (Q)_{U(\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}')} \bigr) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \bigr\|\,.

   987	\begin{lemma}[Consistency and approximate commutation of the expanded point measurements]
   988		\label{lem:qld-comm-cons}
   989		\uses{def:expanded-point-measurement, def:expanded-point-trace-projection, def:expanded-state, def:approx-question-indexed-operators, def:povm-distance, def:symmetric-equivalents}
   990		There exists a function $\delta_{\mathrm{Anticom}}(\eps) = \poly(\eps)$
   991		such that the following holds, with respect to the state
   992		$\ket{\hat{\psi}}$ of Definition~\ref{def:expanded-state}.
   993		\begin{enumerate}
   994			\item (\textbf{Self-consistency}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, on
   995			average over $r \in \F_q$ and $u \in \F_q^m$ (the relation does not
   996			depend on $r$), we have
   997			\[
   998				(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
   999				\,\approx_\eps\,
  1000				(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,,
  1001			\]
  1002			where the answer summation is over $a \in \F_q$.
  1003			\item (\textbf{Approximate commutation}) For all $b, b' \in \F_2$,
  1004			on average over uniformly random
  1005			$\omega = (u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z) \in (\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$, we
  1006			have
  1007			\[
  1008				(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),u_X,r_X}_{b}\,
  1009				\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),u_Z,r_Z}_{b'})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
  1010				\,\approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{Anticom}}}\,
  1011				(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),u_Z,r_Z}_{b'}\,
  1012				\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),u_X,r_X}_{b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}\,.
  1013			\]
  1014		\end{enumerate}
  1015		Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations also
  1016		hold, and the proof yields $\delta_{\mathrm{Anticom}}(\eps) = \sqrt{\eps}$.
  1017	\end{lemma}
  1018	\begin{proof}
  1019		\uses{lem:qld-win-implications, lem:qld-win-implications-obs, fact:data-processing, lem:twisted-commutation, def:expanded-point-measurement, def:expanded-point-trace-projection, def:expanded-observables, lem:symmetric-equivalents-transfer}
  1020		For item~1: the original point measurements
  1021		$\{M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\}$ are $\eps$-self-consistent between
  1022		registers $\mathsf{A}$ and $\mathsf{B}$ in $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$
  1023		(item~\ref{enu:qld-cons} of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}), the
  1024		Pauli projections $\{\tau^{W,u}_a\}$ are perfectly self-consistent
  1025		between registers $\mathsf{A}'$ and $\mathsf{A}''$ on the EPR ancillas,
  1026		and the data processing inequality (Lemma~\ref{fact:data-processing})
  1027		combines the two through the convolution form of
  1028		Definition~\ref{def:expanded-point-measurement}. For item~2:
  1029		by~\eqref{eq:lc-22}, each side expands as
  1030		$\frac14 \big( \Id + (-1)^b \hat{X}^{r_X}(u_X) + (-1)^{b'} \hat{Z}^{r_Z}(u_Z) + (-1)^{b+b'} \hat{X}^{r_X}(u_X) \hat{Z}^{r_Z}(u_Z) \big)$
  1031		respectively its reverse-ordered analogue, so it suffices to commute
  1032		the two expanded observables. By~\eqref{eq:lc-23},
  1033		$\hat{X}^{r_X}(u_X)\hat{Z}^{r_Z}(u_Z) = X^{r_X}(u_X) Z^{r_Z}(u_Z) \ot \tau^X(r_X \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_X)) \tau^Z(r_Z \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_Z))$;
  1034		the strategy observables approximately commute or anticommute with sign
  1035		$(-1)^{\gamma(\omega)}$ and error $\sqrt{\eps}$
  1036		(\eqref{eq:pts-obs-commutation} of
  1037		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications-obs}), while the generalized Pauli
  1038		observables exactly commute or anticommute with the same sign

  1040		$\hat{X}^{r_X}(u_X)\hat{Z}^{r_Z}(u_Z) \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} \hat{Z}^{r_Z}(u_Z)\hat{X}^{r_X}(u_X)$
  1041		on average over uniformly random $\omega$, giving the approximate
  1042		commutation with $\delta_{\mathrm{Anticom}} = \sqrt{\eps}$. The
  1043		symmetric equivalents follow from
  1044		Lemma~\ref{lem:symmetric-equivalents-transfer}.
  1045	\end{proof}

   365	\label{sec:expanding}

   371	$\alice' \alice''$ and $\bob' \bob''$; recall also that the state $\ket{\psi}$ is already implicitly  appended with sufficiently many ancilla qubits initialized in the $\ket{0}$ state.

   434	\paragraph{Partitioning the registers, and symmetries}
   435	In the remainder of this section as well as \Cref{sec:combining,sec:apply-ldt}, we will partition the six registers
   436	$\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''$ into
   437	two ``parties'' in two different ways. The first is to consider
   438	$\alice \alice'$ together to form  a single party, and $\bob \alice''$
   439	to form the second party. The second is to consider $\bob \bob'$ to
   440	form the first party, and $\alice \bob''$ to form the second
   441	party. Thanks to the symmetry of the Pauli basis test under exchanging the
   442	two players, as well as the symmetry of the ancilla states in
   443	registers $\alice' \alice''$ and $\bob' \bob''$, every ``bipartite'' consistency relation we derive between two
   444	operators $M, N$ will hold for both of the two bipartitioning schemes,
   445	and with the first and second party interchanged. That is, whenever we
   446	derive a bipartite relation of the form
   447	\[ M_{\alice \alice'} \approx_\delta N_{\bob \alice''}, \]
   448	the same steps, with the registers appropriately changed, will also
   449	yield
   450	\begin{align*}
   451	  N_{\alice \alice'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\bob \alice''}, \\
   452	  M_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} N_{\alice \bob''}, \\
   453	  N_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\alice \bob''}.
   454	\end{align*}
   455	
   456	Similarly, whenever we derive a single-party relation of the form
   457	$M_{\alice \alice'} \approx N_{\alice \alice'}$, the same steps with
   458	the registers appropriately changed will also yield the same relation
   459	on $\bob\alice''$, $\bob \bob'$ and $\alice \bob''$. We refer to these
   460	relations as \emph{symmetric equivalents}.

   592		bounded below by a universal constant.

   594		and~\ref{enu:qld-pauli-basis-cons} then follow directly from the
   595		corresponding subtests and the assumption that $\mathcal{S}$ succeeds
   596		with probability at least $1-\eps$, where item~\ref{enu:qld-ld} follows
   597		from the consistency subtest of the low individual degree game executed
   598		inside the Pauli basis test. In more detail for item~\ref{enu:qld-ld}:
   599		the disagreement mass of the two completed families is rejection mass
   600		of the line-versus-point clauses
   601		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-win-predicate}, invoked by the low-degree
   602		check of Definition~\ref{def:pauli-win-predicate}). An outcome pair
   603		$(a,b)$ with $a \neq b$ in $\F_q$ is a line answer evaluating at $u$
   604		to $a$ against the point answer $b$, which the clause rejects; a pair
   605		$(\bot,b)$ is a line answer with no evaluation at $u$, which the
   606		universally quantified clause rejects against every point answer $b$
   607		(Remark~\ref{rem:ld-win-zero-direction} and
   608		Remark~\ref{rem:deg-line-representatives}); and the pairs $(a,\bot)$
   609		contribute no mass, since the class
   610		$M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{\bot}$ is the zero operator. The subtests underlying
   611		items~\ref{enu:qld-comm} and~\ref{enu:qld-comm-cons} accept vacuously
   612		unless the sampled tuple $\omega$ is commuting, and those underlying
   613		items~\ref{enu:qld-ms} and~\ref{enu:qld-ms-cons} accept vacuously
   614		unless $\omega$ is anticommuting. Since the parameter tuple $(q,m,d)$
   615		is admissible (Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), $m$ divides $q$, so
   616		$1 \leq m \leq q$, and Lemma~\ref{fact:omega-anticomm-prob} shows that
   617		a uniformly sampled tuple $\omega$ is commuting with probability at
   618		least $\frac12$ and anticommuting with probability at least $2^{-4}$.
   619		Conditioning on either event therefore increases the failure
   620		probability of the corresponding subtest by a factor of at most $2^4$,
   621		and items~\ref{enu:qld-comm},~\ref{enu:qld-comm-cons}
   622		and~\ref{enu:qld-ms-cons} follow from the corresponding subtests.
   623		Item~\ref{enu:qld-ms} follows in the same way, because the Magic Square
   624		check is executed with constant probability over the choice of a pair
   625		of questions and the anticommuting event has probability at least
   626		$2^{-4}$. Finally, that all approximations
   627		also hold with $\approx_\eps$ in place of $\simeq_\eps$ is immediate
   628		from Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement}.
   629	\end{proof}
   630	
   631	\begin{lemma}[Winning implications for observables]
   632		\label{lem:qld-win-implications-obs}
   633		% The source labels this lemma `len:qld-win-implications-obs'; the prefix
   634		% `len' is a typo for `lem'. The label above is the corrected form.
   635		\uses{def:strategy-observables, def:approx-question-indexed-operators, def:anticommuting-tuple, lem:projective-strategy-setup}
   636		The following hold for the observables $W^r(u)$ of
   637		Definition~\ref{def:strategy-observables}, with respect to the state
   638		$\ket{\psi}$ of the strategy under analysis
   639		(Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-strategy-setup} and the convention
   640		following it).
   641		\begin{enumerate}
   642			\item For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and $r \in \F_q$, on average over
   643			uniformly random $u \in \F_q^m$,
   644			\begin{equation}\label{eq:pts-obs-consistency}
   645				W^r(u) \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}} \,\approx_\eps\, \Id_{\mathsf{A}} \ot W^r(u)\,.
   646			\end{equation}
   647			\item On average over uniformly random
   648			$\omega = (u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z) \in (\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$,
   649			\begin{equation}\label{eq:pts-obs-commutation}
   650				X^{r_X}(u_X)\, Z^{r_Z}(u_Z) \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}}
   651				\,\approx_{\sqrt{\eps}}\,
   652				(-1)^{\gamma(\omega)}\, Z^{r_Z}(u_Z)\, X^{r_X}(u_X) \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}}\,,
   653			\end{equation}
   654			where
   655			$\gamma(\omega) = \tr((r_X \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_X)) \cdot (r_Z \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_Z)))$
   656			as in Definition~\ref{def:anticommuting-tuple}.
   657		\end{enumerate}
   658		Furthermore, all of the approximations above also hold with the tensor
   659		factors interchanged.
   660	\end{lemma}
   661	\begin{proof}
   662		\uses{lem:qld-win-implications, lem:povm-to-obs, fact:data-processing, fact:agreement, lem:commutation-analysis, thm:ms-rigidity, fact:add-a-proj, def:strategy-observables}
   663		For~\eqref{eq:pts-obs-consistency}: item~\ref{enu:qld-cons} of
   664		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} and the data processing inequality
   665		(Lemma~\ref{fact:data-processing}), using that the type
   666		$(\mathrm{Point},W)$ is sampled with constant probability, give the
   667		self-consistency of the coarse-grained measurements
   668		$\{M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{[\tr(\cdot\,r)=a]}\}_{a \in \F_2}$ on
   669		average over $u$; Lemma~\ref{lem:povm-to-obs}, applied with
   670		$\mathcal{A} = \F_2$ and $\alpha_a = (-1)^a$, converts this
   671		to~\eqref{eq:pts-obs-consistency}. For the commuting case
   672		of~\eqref{eq:pts-obs-commutation}: chaining
   673		items~\ref{enu:qld-comm-cons},~\ref{enu:qld-comm}
   674		and~\ref{enu:qld-cons} of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} via
   675		Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement} gives, on average over commuting $\omega$,
   676		$M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u_W}_{[\tr(\cdot\,r_W)=a]} \ot \Id_{\mathsf{B}} \approx_\eps \Id_{\mathsf{A}} \ot M^{\mathrm{Pair},\omega}_{[\beta_W=a]}$;
   677		since the measurement
   678		$\{M^{\mathrm{Pair},\omega}_{\beta_X,\beta_Z}\}$ is projective,
   679		Lemma~\ref{lem:commutation-analysis}, applied with the $X$- and
   680		$Z$-point projections and the $\mathrm{Pair}$ measurement, yields the
   681		approximate commutation of the projections
   682		$M^{(\mathrm{Point},X),u_X}_{[\tr(\cdot\,r_X)=b]}$ and
   683		$M^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),u_Z}_{[\tr(\cdot\,r_Z)=c]}$; expanding
   684		$W^r(u) = \Id - 2 M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{[\tr(\cdot\,r)=1]}$
   685		transfers this to the observables with error $\eps$. For the
   686		anticommuting case: item~\ref{enu:qld-ms-cons} of
   687		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} together with
   688		Lemma~\ref{lem:povm-to-obs} relates $X^{r_X}(u_X)$ and $Z^{r_Z}(u_Z)$
   689		to the Magic Square observables
   690		$M^{\mathrm{Variable}_j,\omega} = M^{\mathrm{Variable}_j,\omega}_0 - M^{\mathrm{Variable}_j,\omega}_1$
   691		for $j \in \{1,5\}$; for each anticommuting $\omega$, the Magic Square
   692		rigidity theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-rigidity}) applied with
   693		$\eps_\omega = 1 - \Lambda_\omega$ gives
   694		$\Id \ot M^{\mathrm{Variable}_1,\omega} M^{\mathrm{Variable}_5,\omega} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps_\omega}} - \Id \ot M^{\mathrm{Variable}_5,\omega} M^{\mathrm{Variable}_1,\omega}$;
   695		averaging over anticommuting $\omega$ with Jensen's inequality
   696		($\E \eps_\omega^{1/2} \leq (\E \eps_\omega)^{1/2} = O(\eps^{1/2})$,
   697		using item~\ref{enu:qld-ms}) and transferring across the tensor factor
   698		with Lemma~\ref{fact:add-a-proj}, applied twice, yields the
   699		anticommutation with error $\sqrt{\eps}$. The two cases combine into
   700		the $(-1)^{\gamma(\omega)}$-signed statement over uniformly random
   701		$\omega$, since the uniform average is bounded by the sum of the two
   702		conditional averages.
   703	\end{proof}
   704	
   705	\begin{remark}[Source corrections]
   706		\label{rem:qld-win-implications-typos}
   707		Two typographical slips in the source are corrected above. In
   708		item~\ref{enu:qld-ms} of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} the
   709		source writes the expectation over $\omega$ subject to the condition
   710		$\tr((r_X \cdot u_X) \cdot (r_Z \cdot u_Z)) \neq 0$, omitting the map
   711		$\mathrm{ind}_m$; the intended condition, consistent with the
   712		surrounding text and with Definition~\ref{def:anticommuting-tuple}, is
   713		$\gamma(\omega) \neq 0$, that is, $\omega$ anticommuting, and this is
   714		the form stated above. In the source proof of
   715		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications-obs}, one display reads
   716		$Z^{r_X}(u_X)\,X^{r_Z}(u_Z)$ where $Z^{r_Z}(u_Z)\,X^{r_X}(u_X)$ is
   717		meant.
   718		% A third slip in the source, the label prefix `len' in place of `lem'
   719		% on the lemma corresponding to lem:qld-win-implications-obs, is
   720		% recorded in the comment at that lemma; no alias label is defined.
   721		In addition, the source proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}
   722		restricts attention to the case $6md \leq q$ and disposes of the
   723		remaining parameters by an appeal to Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}, the
   724		theorem whose proof the lemma is part of; that argument does not
   725		establish the unrestricted statement of the lemma, and for $d = 0$ the
   726		probability bound it invokes is false
   727		(Remark~\ref{rem:omega-anticomm-prob-correction}). The proof given
   728		above instead uses the lower bounds of
   729		Lemma~\ref{fact:omega-anticomm-prob} on the probabilities of the
   730		commuting and anticommuting events, which are universal constants for
   731		every admissible parameter tuple, so no restriction on the parameters
   732		is needed.
   733		Finally, the source states item~\ref{enu:qld-ld} of
   734		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} with answer summation over
   735		$a \in \F_q$ only, implicitly reading the evaluation classes of the
   736		line measurement as a complete measurement. Under the coefficient
   737		reading of Definition~\ref{def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
   738		(Remark~\ref{rem:deg-line-representatives}) the classes indexed by
   739		$a \in \F_q$ form only a sub-measurement when the line has zero
   740		direction --- a case the question distribution produces with positive
   741		probability (Remark~\ref{rem:ld-win-zero-direction}) --- while the
   742		relation $\simeq_\eps$ of Definition~\ref{def:consistency} is defined
   743		for POVMs. Item~\ref{enu:qld-ld} therefore completes both families by
   744		an explicit $\bot$ outcome; the same implicit completeness assumption
   745		occurs in the source proof of the statement corresponding to
   746		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-line-cons}, whose proof below invokes the
   747		completed families instead.
   748	\end{remark}

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Consistency
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.StrategyClasses
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Observables.LineDefs
+
+/-!
+# Low-degree game interfaces
+
+This file supplies the finite polynomial-measurement index and the imported
+soundness provider required by the QPBT combining argument.  Polynomial
+outcomes are the actual bounded `polyFunc` representatives.
+
+## References
+
+The source-facing declarations are `def:ld-meas` and `lem:ld-soundness` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:112-178`.  Their paper origin is
+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:392-480`.
+The imported-provider gap is documented in
+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT
+open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
+open MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-- The bounded multivariate polynomial outcome used by the low-degree
+soundness theorem. -/
+abbrev PolyIndex (L : LdParams) := ↥(polyFunc L.m (ScalarQ L) L.d)
+
+/-- A simultaneous tuple of `L.k` bounded polynomial representatives. -/
+abbrev PolyTuple (L : LdParams) := Fin L.k → PolyIndex L
+
+/-- A complete POVM indexed by simultaneous bounded polynomial outcomes. -/
+abbrev PolyMeasTuple (L : LdParams) (ι : Type*)
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] := Measurement (PolyTuple L) ι
+
+/-- Evaluate every component of a polynomial tuple at a point. -/
+def evalPolyTupleAt {L : LdParams} (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
+    (g : PolyTuple L) : Fin L.k → ScalarQ L :=
+  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
+
+/-- Completed evaluation used to post-process a polynomial measurement. -/
+def evalPolyTupleAtOpt {L : LdParams} (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
+    (g : PolyTuple L) : Option (Fin L.k → ScalarQ L) :=
+  some (evalPolyTupleAt u g)
+
+/-- Extract a point-value tuple from a low-degree answer, using `none` for an
+answer of the wrong constructor. -/
+def pointAnswerOpt {L : LdParams} (a : LdAnswer L) :
+    Option (Fin L.k → ScalarQ L) :=
+  match a with
+  | .pointVals values => some values
+  | _ => none
+
+/-- Embed a geometric point into the ambient coefficient space used by a
+point question.  This is formalization-only question infrastructure. -/
+def pointSpaceOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdSpace L :=
+  fun i => match i with
+  | .inl (.inl j) => u j
+  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
+  | .inr _ => 0
+
+/-- The typed low-degree point question associated with `u`. -/
+def ldPointQuestionOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdQuestion L :=
+  (.point, pointSpaceOf L u)
+
+/-- Alice's point measurement, completed by an explicit `none` outcome for
+answers of the wrong constructor. -/
+noncomputable def pointMeasurementA {L : LdParams} (S : Strategy (ldGame L))
+    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :
+    Measurement (Option (Fin L.k → ScalarQ L)) S.ιA :=
+  (S.A (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess pointAnswerOpt
+
+/-- Bob's completed point measurement. -/
+noncomputable def pointMeasurementB {L : LdParams} (S : Strategy (ldGame L))
+    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :
+    Measurement (Option (Fin L.k → ScalarQ L)) S.ιB :=
+  (S.B (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess pointAnswerOpt
+
+/-- The quantitative error function in `lem:ld-soundness`.  Its argument order
+is `(a, b, ε, q, m, d, k)`. -/
+noncomputable def deltaLd (a b ε : ℝ) (q m d k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
+  a * Real.rpow (((d * m * k : ℕ) : ℝ)) a *
+    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
+      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
+
+/-- Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree
+test (`lem:ld-soundness`, blueprint lines 125--178; paper origin
+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:392-480`).
+
+The `Option` completion makes malformed point answers explicit on both sides
+of the first two relations.  It adds no hypothesis and agrees with the game's
+rejection convention.
+
+**Unfaithful:** This imported proof remains open because the asserted game
+correspondence and the provider's auxiliary-parameter bound have not been
+derived.  They are documented in
+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.  Elimination: prove the
+typed-game reduction and repair the parameter choice, then instantiate the
+low-individual-degree soundness provider.
+-/
+theorem exists_ld_soundness :
+    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
+      ∀ (L : LdParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
+        ∀ S : Strategy (ldGame L), S.IsProjective → 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
+          ∃ GA : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιA, ∃ GB : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιB,
+            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
+                (fun u outcome =>
+                  heteroKron ((pointMeasurementA S u).effect outcome) 1)
+                (fun u outcome =>
+                  heteroKron 1
+                    ((GB.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAtOpt u)).effect outcome))
+                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
+            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
+                (fun u outcome =>
+                  heteroKron
+                    ((GA.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAtOpt u)).effect outcome) 1)
+                (fun u outcome =>
+                  heteroKron 1 ((pointMeasurementB S u).effect outcome))
+                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
+            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+                (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
+                (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
+                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k := by
+  sorry
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.PauliBasisTest

/-!
# Pauli basis test soundness

The quantitative error function and the source-shaped soundness statement live
here.  All analytic estimates are intentionally proof-level obligations in the
stage-4.1 skeleton; the carriers below are concrete finite-dimensional vectors
and matrices so that later proofs can use the existing Hilbert-space API.

## References

The main declaration is `thm:pauli` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
The distance functionals use `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` from
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT
open MIPStarRE.Quantum

noncomputable section

/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
as specified by `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`,
paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
-/
noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))

/-- Matrix conjugation by a finite-dimensional linear isometry.  This is a
Lean-only helper for the operator conclusion of `thm:pauli`; it uses the
matrix representation of the isometry and its conjugate transpose.  Blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
-/
noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
  U * M * Uᴴ

/-- Reindex a finite Euclidean-space vector along an equivalence.  This is the
coordinate form of the tensor-register shuffle used in the paper's ideal
state (`def:EPR`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`),
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`.
-/
noncomputable def reindexState {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (e : ι ≃ ι')
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι' :=
  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm
    (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))

/-- Coordinate tensoring of two local maps on a bipartite state.  The formula
is a genuine finite sum over the input coordinates; preservation of the norm
is part of the later soundness proof for `thm:pauli`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
-/
noncomputable def isometryTensor
    {ιA ιB ιA' ιB' R : Type*}
    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA'] [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × R))
    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × R))
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) :=
  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) ℂ).symm
    (fun p =>
      ∑ i : ιA, ∑ j : ιB,
        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × R) ℂ)
            (φA ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιA ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) p.1) *
          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιB' × R) ℂ)
            (φB ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιB ℂ).symm (Pi.single j 1))) p.2) *
          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA × ιB) ℂ) ψ (i, j)) )

/-- The ideal auxiliary state `aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}` in the shuffled register
ordering.  The EPR factor is the concrete `eprState` from
`def:EPR` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`; paper
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`).
-/
noncomputable def idealState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) ×
      (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    (fun p =>
      ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ) aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P) ℂ)
          (eprState (PauliRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))

/-- The Pauli question carrying no additional coefficient data, as in
`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`.
-/

  (.pauli W, 0)

in `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).

    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
  fun p q =>
    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
      pauliProj W u p.1.2 q.1.2
    else 0

/-- The symmetric B-side ideal Pauli projector from `thm:pauli`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.

noncomputable def pauliProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
  fun p q =>
    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
      pauliProj W u p.2.2 q.2.2

    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']

  fun p q =>
    if p.2 = q.2 then
      (conjIsometry φA M) p.1 q.1
    else 0

    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']

      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
    (M : Op S.ιB) :
    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
  fun p q =>
    if p.1 = q.1 then
      (conjIsometry φB M) p.2 q.2
    else 0

data in the paper theorem; it introduces no extra hypothesis.  Blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
-/
structure PauliSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
  ιA' : Type
  ιB' : Type
  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P)
  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P)
  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1

attribute [instance] PauliSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype
