/-- The A-side operator-distance quantity appearing in the soundness
conclusion.  It is the finite-sum realization of `def:povm-distance` from
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
-/
noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceA
    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA
        ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
      pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2

/-- The symmetric B-side operator-distance quantity from `def:povm-distance`,
blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
-/
noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceB
    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedBEffect S w.φB
        ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
      pauliProjOnB'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2

/-- `thm:pauli`: every sufficiently successful Pauli basis test strategy admits
local isometries and an auxiliary unit state for which the state and both
operator families are close at scale `deltaQld`.  The theorem uses the
once-and-for-all self-dual-normal field model selected by `fixedFieldModel` for
each admissible size, rather than a freshly quantified field identification.
Blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.

The paper's asymptotic constants are encoded by the explicit `deltaQld`
functional; the squared operator distances use the quantitative convention of
`def:povm-distance` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`).
-/
theorem pauli_soundness :
    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
          ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,
            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤
                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
            (∀ W : PauliKind,
              pauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
            (∀ W : PauliKind,
              pauliOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) := by
  sorry

end

§7 + the "Analysis of the Pauli basis test" appendix; secondary
arXiv:1904.05870) in Lean 4, using the fully local agent workflow in

recording telemetry throughout as data for a research paper on
self-evolving formalization workflows.

## Hard-won operational lessons (do not relearn these)

- Fill issue/PR record bodies — the reviewer audits them (twice flagged).
- Review loop: cap at 4 rounds, then §12 adjudication; reviewers have no
  memory across rounds and unbounded depth on new text.
- Byte-capped truncation of UTF-8 must repair the decode boundary
  (dispatch.sh does now); reproduce failures with the REAL payload.
- Machine-wide full-build mutex: `$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock`; a live
  owner is never broken. Single-file `lake env lean` needs no lock.
- Hot cache: only `cache-warmer.sh` writes snapshots; worktrees consume
  via `worktree-setup.sh`; never `lake update`.
- Pass large agent inputs by file path; never inline huge JSON.
- events.md → EVOLUTION.md is the amendment pipeline; cite triggers.

as submodules (pointer bumps are occasional and owner-driven). Track B

12 protocol amendments. Keep the same discipline; the model-family switch

    88	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    89	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    90	
    91	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    92	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    93	-/
    94	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
    95	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
    96	
    97	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    98	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    99	-/
   100	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   101	  fun i => z (.inr i)
   102	
   103	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   104	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   107	-/
   108	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   109	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   110	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   111	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   112	
   113	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   114	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   115	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   116	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   117	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   118	-/
   119	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   120	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   121	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   122	
   123	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   124	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   125	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   126	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   127	-/
   128	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   129	  fun i => match i with
   130	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   131	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   132	  | .inr _ => 0
   133	
   134	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   135	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   136	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   137	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   138	-/
   139	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   140	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   141	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   142	  fun i => match i with
   143	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   144	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   145	  | .inr _ => 0
   146	
   147	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   148	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   149	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   150	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper origin
   151	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   152	-/
   153	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   154	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   155	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   156	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   157	  fun i => match i with
   158	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   159	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   160	  | .inr j => direction j
   161	
   162	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   163	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   164	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   165	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   166	-/
   167	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   168	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   169	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   170	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P
   171	
   172	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the affine-line map.  This is a named
   173	Lean proof obligation for the prose assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`,
   174	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper
   175	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   176	-/
   177	theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
   178	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
   179	  sorry
   180	
   181	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the diagonal-line map.  This is the
   182	level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   183	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   184	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   185	-/
   186	theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
   187	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by
   188	  sorry
   189	
   190	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   191	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
   192	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   193	-/
   194	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   195	
   196	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   197	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   198	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   199	-/
   200	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   201	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   202	  Distribution.map
   203	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   204	    (fun s =>
   205	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   206	
   207	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   208	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   209	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   210	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
   211	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   212	-/
   213	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   214	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   215	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   216	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   217	  deriving DecidableEq
   218	
   219	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   220	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   221	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   222	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   223	-/
   224	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   225	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   226	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   227	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   228	
   229	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   230	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   231	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   232	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   233	-/
   234	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   235	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   236	  toFun
   237	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   238	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   239	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   240	  invFun
   241	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   242	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   243	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   244	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   245	  right_inv := by
   246	    intro x
   247	    cases x with
   248	    | inl a => rfl
   249	    | inr x =>
   250	        cases x with
   251	        | inl a => rfl
   252	        | inr a => rfl
   253	
   254	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   255	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
   256	
   257	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   258	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   259	
   260	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   261	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   262	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   263	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   264	-/
   265	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   266	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   267	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   268	
   269	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   270	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   271	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   272	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   273	-/
   274	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   275	  match t, a with
   276	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   277	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   278	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   279	  | _, _ => false
   280	
   281	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   282	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   283	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   284	-/
   285	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   286	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   287	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   288	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   289	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   290	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   291	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   292	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   293	
   294	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   295	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   296	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   297	-/
   298	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   299	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   300	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   301	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   302	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   303	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   304	
   305	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   306	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   307	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   308	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   309	-/
   310	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   311	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   312	  open Classical in
   313	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   314	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   315	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   316	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   317	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   318	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   319	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   320	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   321	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   322	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   323	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   324	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   325	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   326	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   327	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   328	      else false
   329	
   330	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   331	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   332	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   333	-/
   334	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   335	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   336	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   337	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   338	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   339	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   340	  μ_prob := by sorry
   341	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   342	
   343	end
   344	
   345	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Lines and canonical representatives
     5	
     6	The classical and Pauli question distributions use affine lines in a finite
     7	coordinate space.  This module keeps the zero-direction case explicit and
     8	provides the canonical projection used for line representatives.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The source-facing nodes are `def:line`, `prop:line-equiv`, and
    13	`def:line-representative` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:433-492`.
    14	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:102-174`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	
    21	variable {K : Type*} [Field K]
    22	
    23	/--
    24	The affine line through `u` in direction `v`, including the singleton case
    25	`v = 0`.  Blueprint `def:line`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:439-453`;
    26	paper origin
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    28	-/
    29	def linePoints {m : ℕ}
    30	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Set (Fin m → K) :=
    31	  {x | ∃ t : K, x = u + t • v}
    32	
    33	/-- The elementary coordinate direction used in the axis-parallel predicate of
    34	`def:line`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:439-453`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    36	-/
    37	def coordinateDirection {m : ℕ}
    38	    (i : Fin m) : Fin m → K :=
    39	  Pi.single i 1
    40	
    41	/--
    42	`IsAxisParallel v` means that `v` is a standard coordinate direction.  This is
    43	the axis-parallel clause of `def:line` (blueprint lines 445-450; paper
    44	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`).
    45	-/
    46	def IsAxisParallel {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    47	  ∃ i : Fin m, v = coordinateDirection i
    48	
    49	/--
    50	The diagonal-direction predicate from `def:line`; a prefix of coordinates may
    51	vanish.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:439-453`; paper origin
    52	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    53	-/
    54	def IsDiagonal {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    55	  ∃ i : Fin m, ∀ j : Fin m, j.1 < i.1 → v j = 0
    56	
    57	/--
    58	Changing the base point to another point on a line leaves the line unchanged.
    59	This is `prop:line-equiv` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:455-466`,
    60	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:128-132`.
    61	-/
    62	theorem linePoints_eq_of_mem {m : ℕ}
    63	    (u v u' : Fin m → K) (h : u' ∈ linePoints u v) :
    64	    linePoints u v = linePoints u' v := by
    65	  sorry
    66	
    67	/--
    68	The canonical linear representative map of a line direction.  It projects onto
    69	the coordinate complement of the span of `v`; for `v = 0` the span is bottom,
    70	so the resulting map is the identity.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`,
    71	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:472-492`; paper origin
    72	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`.
    73	-/
    74	noncomputable def lineRepMap {m : ℕ}
    75	    (v : Fin m → K) : (Fin m → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin m → K) :=
    76	  canonicalProjOfKernel (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)))
    77	
    78	/- The point-valued companion to `lineRepMap`; Lean-only notation for the
    79	canonical representative in `def:line-representative`. -/
    80	/-- The canonical representative point `lineRepMap v u`.  Blueprint
    81	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:472-492`, paper origin
    82	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:166-174`.
    83	-/
    84	noncomputable def lineRep {m : ℕ}
    85	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Fin m → K :=
    86	  lineRepMap v u
    87	
    88	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# The low-degree encoding
     5	
     6	This module encodes the Boolean subcube by multilinear indicator polynomials
     7	and packages the resulting low-degree code as honest polynomial representatives.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The source-facing nodes are `def:polynomials-degree`,
    12	`def:low-degree-encoding`, and `def:indicator-vector` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:321-417`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    15	The polynomial class `def:polyfunc` is reused from
    16	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc` (the LDT formalization).
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	open MvPolynomial
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	/- The Boolean cube indexes the `2^m` qudits in the low-degree encoding. -/
    25	/-- The Boolean cube indexing the `2^m` qudits of the test.  This is the index
    26	type in `def:low-degree-encoding`, blueprint
    27	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    28	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    29	-/
    30	abbrev Cube (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bool
    31	
    32	/--
    33	The representative polynomial which is `1` at `y` on the Boolean cube and
    34	zero at the other cube points.  This is the indicator polynomial in
    35	`def:low-degree-encoding` (blueprint lines 381-401; paper
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`).
    37	-/
    38	noncomputable def indicatorPoly {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ} (y : Cube m) :
    39	    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    40	  ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then X i else (1 - X i)
    41	
    42	/--
    43	The multilinear low-degree encoding of a coefficient string.  Polynomial
    44	representatives are used, as fixed by issue #0004, rather than quotienting by
    45	functional equality.  Blueprint: `def:low-degree-encoding`,
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`; paper origin:
    47	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    48	-/
    49	noncomputable def lowDegreeEncoding {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    50	    (a : Cube m → K) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    51	  ∑ y : Cube m, a y • indicatorPoly y
    52	
    53	/- Evaluation shorthand for the representative polynomial in
    54	`def:low-degree-encoding`; it is Lean-only notation. -/
    55	/-- Evaluation shorthand for the low-degree encoding.  Blueprint
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    60	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) : K :=
    61	  eval x (lowDegreeEncoding a)
    62	
    63	/--
    64	The indicator vector `ind_m(x)` of `def:indicator-vector`.
    65	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`; paper origin:
    66	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    67	-/
    68	noncomputable def indicatorVec {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    69	    (x : Fin m → K) : Cube m → K :=
    70	  fun y => eval x (indicatorPoly y)
    71	
    72	/--
    73	The defining dot-product identity for the encoding, corresponding to
    74	Equation `eq:low-degree-encoding-definition` and `lem:indicator-vector` in the
    75	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`, paper origin
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    77	It is a proof obligation in stage 4.1.
    78	-/
    79	theorem lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}

     4	# Lines and canonical representatives
     5	
     6	The classical and Pauli question distributions use affine lines in a finite
     7	coordinate space.  This module keeps the zero-direction case explicit and
     8	provides the canonical projection used for line representatives.
     9

    11

    22

    24	The affine line through `u` in direction `v`, including the singleton case
    25	`v = 0`.  Blueprint `def:line`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:439-453`;
    26	paper origin
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    28	-/
    29	def linePoints {m : ℕ}
    30	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Set (Fin m → K) :=
    31	  {x | ∃ t : K, x = u + t • v}
    32	
    33	/-- The elementary coordinate direction used in the axis-parallel predicate of
    34	`def:line`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:439-453`, paper origin

    36	-/
    37	def coordinateDirection {m : ℕ}

    40	
    41	/--
    42	`IsAxisParallel v` means that `v` is a standard coordinate direction.  This is
    43	the axis-parallel clause of `def:line` (blueprint lines 445-450; paper
    44	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`).
    45	-/
    46	def IsAxisParallel {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=

    53	-/

     3	/-!
     4	# The low-degree encoding
     5	
     6	This module encodes the Boolean subcube by multilinear indicator polynomials
     7	and packages the resulting low-degree code as honest polynomial representatives.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The source-facing nodes are `def:polynomials-degree`,
    12	`def:low-degree-encoding`, and `def:indicator-vector` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:321-417`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    15	The polynomial class `def:polyfunc` is reused from
    16	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc` (the LDT formalization).
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	open MvPolynomial
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	/- The Boolean cube indexes the `2^m` qudits in the low-degree encoding. -/
    25	/-- The Boolean cube indexing the `2^m` qudits of the test.  This is the index
    26	type in `def:low-degree-encoding`, blueprint
    27	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    28	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    29	-/
    30	abbrev Cube (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bool
    31	
    32	/--
    33	The representative polynomial which is `1` at `y` on the Boolean cube and
    34	zero at the other cube points.  This is the indicator polynomial in
    35	`def:low-degree-encoding` (blueprint lines 381-401; paper
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`).
    37	-/
    38	noncomputable def indicatorPoly {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ} (y : Cube m) :
    39	    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    40	  ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then X i else (1 - X i)
    41	
    42	/--
    43	The multilinear low-degree encoding of a coefficient string.  Polynomial
    44	representatives are used, as fixed by issue #0004, rather than quotienting by
    45	functional equality.  Blueprint: `def:low-degree-encoding`,
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`; paper origin:
    47	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    48	-/
    49	noncomputable def lowDegreeEncoding {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    50	    (a : Cube m → K) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    51	  ∑ y : Cube m, a y • indicatorPoly y
    52	
    53	/- Evaluation shorthand for the representative polynomial in

    55	/-- Evaluation shorthand for the low-degree encoding.  Blueprint
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    60	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) : K :=
    61	  eval x (lowDegreeEncoding a)
    62	
    63	/--
    64	The indicator vector `ind_m(x)` of `def:indicator-vector`.
    65	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`; paper origin:
